report.summary: Chunk 2 of slice.py: contains _reverse_import_map, _assemble_slice, _fit_budget, and semantic_slice docstring with many claims; code for first three functions is present and checkable.

_assemble_slice | low | Claim of byte-for-byte reproduction of old flat join when full neighbor list and no marker; depends on exact emission order and absence of extra whitespace. | Confirm with test on known input.

_fit_budget | medium | Marker token cost counted each pass, but estimate_tokens is imported; if estimate_tokens is inaccurate, budget fitting may misbehave. | Verify estimate_tokens behavior with edge cases.

semantic_slice | high | Many claims about lanes, withholding, reduction_pct, whole_repo_tokens_exact, and Tier-2 comparison cannot be verified from this chunk alone. | Review full function body and referenced modules.
todos: Verify estimate_tokens function in tokens module.
Check semantic_slice function body (chunk 3+) for implementation of lane logic, withholding, and reduction_pct calculation.
Confirm that _reverse_import_map's fallback matches precomputed order exactly.

handoff.purpose: Contains helper functions _reverse_import_map, _assemble_slice, _fit_budget, and the docstring for semantic_slice.

symbols.name: _reverse_import_map
symbols.note: Builds reverse import map from forward edges; uses precomputed 'import_edges_reverse' if present, else fallback that iterates sorted(edges).

symbols.name: _assemble_slice
symbols.note: Joins focus block, neighbor units with section headers, withheld lines, and optional trimmed marker into a single string.

symbols.name: _fit_budget
symbols.note: Degrades neighbor list by dropping whole units until token budget fits; always keeps focus and withheld block.

symbols.name: semantic_slice
symbols.note: Docstring only; function body not in this chunk. Assembles semantic slice of target with lane-based egress gates, withholding reporting, and budget fitting.

claims.text: The fallback below exists only for an index dict that predates the key (an older JSON dump); it iterates sorted() so the appended caller lists come out in the same order as the precomputed ones.
claims.why: The fallback code at lines 136-142 uses sorted(edges) and setdefault, producing deterministic order matching the claim.

claims.text: A section header is emitted once, and only for a section that still has a kept unit -- so dropping every unit of a section drops its header too.
claims.why: _assemble_slice tracks last_section and only appends header when section differs, so if no neighbor of a section remains, its header is not emitted.

claims.text: With the full neighbour list and no marker this reproduces the old flat join byte-for-byte (the un-budgeted path is unchanged).
claims.why: The 'old flat join' is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify byte-for-byte reproduction without prior code.

claims.text: FOCUS and the WITHHELD block are always kept (a tail truncation would silently delete the anti-hallucination breadcrumb, the exact failure the gate prevents).
claims.why: _fit_budget only modifies the kept list (neighbors), never touches focus_block or withheld_lines; they are passed through unchanged.

claims.text: Lowest keep-priority goes first (callers/signatures before dependency and callee bodies); within a tier the later-emitted unit goes first, so the earliest / most-relevant neighbour survives longest.
claims.why: The keep priority (keep field) is set by the callers of _fit_budget; this chunk does not show how keep values are assigned.

claims.text: The TRIMMED marker's own cost is counted each pass so the kept set fits WITH the marker present.
claims.why: In the while loop, marker is constructed (line 171) and then estimate_tokens is called on the assembled slice including the marker (line 175).

claims.text: ``lane`` selects the egress gate applied to every file that contributes text to ``slice_text`` (see ``sensitivity.slice_egress_rule``).
claims.why: The logic using lane is not in this chunk; sensitivity.slice_egress_rule is not defined here.

claims.text: ``"untrusted"`` -- a genuinely untrusted external provider (DeepSeek). Floor + the existing default-deny allow-list both apply.
claims.why: The allow-list logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Withholding is REPORTED, never silent: the result gains a sorted ``withheld`` block (path, role, rule) AND an inline ``# ===== WITHHELD ... =====`` breadcrumb in ``slice_text`` so the consuming model sees the gap rather than hallucinating the missing callee.
claims.why: The withholding mechanism is not implemented in this chunk; only the withheld_lines parameter is passed through.

claims.text: If the FOCUS file itself is denied the slice fails closed -- no neighbour slice is returned in its place.
claims.why: Not shown in this chunk; likely in semantic_slice body.

claims.text: ``reduction_pct`` is ``1 - slice_tokens / whole_repo_tokens``. Both sides are now counted by the SAME tokenizer (``tokens.count_tokens``: tiktoken cl100k_base when installed, chars/4 otherwise); the denominator used to be a bare ``total_chars // 4`` regardless, so the ratio mixed a measured numerator with an estimated denominator.
claims.why: reduction_pct calculation not in this chunk; tokens.count_tokens not defined here.

claims.text: ``whole_repo_tokens_exact`` is False when that old estimate is still in play (an index dict lacking ``total_tokens`` -- an older JSON dump, or the Rust engine).

``whole_repo_tokens`` is the summed token count of the IN-CENTER source files -- exactly the file set ``index`` accumulates inside its metric-withholding guard, so .daedalusignore'd and out-of-scope files are excluded from the baseline just as they are from the slice.

It is deliberately NOT identical to what ``eval/harness.py:_whole_repo_text`` concatenates for the Tier-2 A/B, which differs in three ways: it prepends a ``# ===== rel =====`` header per file (so its total runs HIGHER), it truncates at a char cap (so on a large repo its total runs LOWER, and it reports ``b_truncated``), and it walks the filesystem with its own ignore-dir list rather than the index's scope, so the two can disagree about which files "the repo" contains.
claims.why: References to eval/harness.py and its behavior are outside this chunk.

claims.text: ``max_tokens`` (default ``None`` -> no cap, byte-identical to before) caps the assembled ``slice_text``. When exceeded the slice degrades by dropping WHOLE neighbour units (never truncating text), always keeping the FOCUS and the WITHHELD block and appending a visible ``# ===== CONTEXT TRIMMED ... =====``
claims.why: _fit_budget implements exactly this: drops whole neighbor units, keeps focus and withheld, appends trimmed marker.

observations.what: _reverse_import_map fallback iterates sorted(edges) to guarantee deterministic order; this is consistent with the docstring claim.
_assemble_slice uses a loop that emits section headers only when section changes; this matches the docstring claim about dropping empty sections.
_fit_budget only modifies the neighbors list; focus_block and withheld_lines are never altered, fulfilling the claim that they are always kept.

The marker string is constructed using an f-string that includes dropped count; its token cost is included in each budget check because estimate_tokens is called on the assembled slice containing the marker.
semantic_slice docstring makes extensive claims about lanes, withholding, reduction_pct, and comparison with eval/harness.py that cannot be verified from this chunk alone.
